claim: *One authoritative representation.* BEFORE — copies A, B, C each feed a consumer and can drift apart, so disagreement is possible. AFTER — one authoritative representation, with A, B, C derived or queried from it, so disagreement becomes detectable or impossible.
topology:
Before: three copies of the same fact each feed a separate consumer, and because each copy can
    change independently, disagreement between them is an ordinary state. After: one authoritative representation
    carries the fact, and the three consumers derive or query it from that single source, so disagreement becomes
    detectable or impossible.
required_terms: Derive / query: disagreement becomes detectable or impossible.
bw_encoding: Black text and strokes, white nodes; boundary weight indicates emphasis or enforcement. Original dashed semantics retained per figure; no color-only distinction.
redesign: Layout reflowed for a 15 cm monochrome print column; color categories replaced by labels and boundary weight.
alt: C.1 Make one source authoritative: from many disagreeing copies to one representation others derive from
